summary.intent: Stop calling `load_verify_locations()` on every verify=True connection by giving verify=True requests a module-level `SSLContext` with the default CA bundle already loaded, and by no longer setting `ca_certs` on the pool in `cert_verify`. Intent source: the supplied pull-request text (psf/requests#6667) and the four commit messages; there is no originating issue, so issue alignment is unavailable.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. The performance goal is met in code, but the shared context changes behaviour the description says is unchanged: it carries client certificates across requests, overrides adapter-level TLS configuration, and loads the bundle at import time.
summary.coverage: The complete merge-base diff of `src/requests/adapters.py` was read, with `HTTPAdapter.send`/`_get_connection`, `docs/user/advanced.rst`, urllib3 2.8.0 `ssl_wrap_socket`/`_merge_pool_kwargs`, and existing TLS-pool tests. Reviewer-executed at the head: `pytest tests/test_requests.py tests/test_adapters.py -k 'ssl or verify or cert or adapter or pool'` gave 21 passed and 3 failed (`test_pyopenssl_redirect`, `test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert`, `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings`); the first two are the known fixture failures, and the third fails identically at the merge-base source (expired fixture certificate). An earlier `-x` run of the same selection stopped at the first known failure. Three local reproductions (client-certificate leak, adapter context override, missing-bundle import) were run at the head and against a `git archive` of the merge-base. The PR's timing claims and live-host checks were not verifiable offline. The change adds no tests. Three candidates were verified in one initial batch, all confirmed; the verifier's statement that it re-ran the scripts is unconfirmed (two tool calls), so the reviewer's own runs are the evidence.

findings.title: Do not load client certificates into the process-wide default SSLContext
findings.trigger: In one process, `requests.get(url_a, verify=True, cert=(certA, keyA))` runs and then `requests.get(url_b, verify=True)` (or a call with a different cert on another thread) runs against a server that asks for a client certificate.
findings.impact: urllib3 calls `context.load_cert_chain()` on the supplied `_preloaded_ssl_context`, so client A's identity stays installed and is presented on later verify=True requests that pass no cert, and concurrent requests with different certs race on one context. Against a local mTLS server the head shows `['clientA', 'clientA', 'clientB', 'clientB']` where the merge-base shows `['clientA', None, 'clientB', None]`.
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context`, pass the shared context only when `client_cert is None`; otherwise set `pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` so urllib3 builds a private context for that pool as before.
findings.source: Pull-request text, "Submitted solution": the change should only avoid a redundant `load_verify_locations()` call.

findings.title: Keep an adapter's own TLS context and settings when verify=True
findings.trigger: An `HTTPAdapter` subclass whose `init_poolmanager` passes `ssl_context=` (or `ssl_version=`, as in `docs/user/advanced.rst`) to `PoolManager` is mounted and used with the default verify=True.
findings.impact: Per-request `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]` overrides the manager's `connection_pool_kw`, so the custom context is never used; cipher or protocol restrictions and legacy-server workarounds silently stop applying. `adapterctx.py` shows `uses custom ctx: False` at the head and `True` at the merge-base.
findings.change: In `_get_connection`/`_urllib3_request_context`, skip adding `ssl_context` when the adapter's pool or proxy manager already defines one in `connection_pool_kw`, and keep the previous CA-bundle handling in that case.

findings.title: Load the default CA bundle lazily, not when requests.adapters is imported
findings.trigger: The certifi bundle path is missing or unreadable, for example a distro-patched certifi in a minimal container or a frozen app without `cacert.pem`.
findings.impact: `import requests` raises `FileNotFoundError`, so programs that only use http, verify=False or an explicit bundle break, and the 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle' message is lost; at the merge-base import succeeded and the error appeared on the first verify=True request. Every import also pays the bundle-parsing cost.
findings.change: Build and cache the default context on the first verify=True request, guarded by a lock, instead of at module level.
